findings: Solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Practice, Book exercises): the Chapter 18 exercise as printed (PDF 133-136, printed 129-132) with answers in English and Roman Urdu: 11 MCQs, 10 short answer, 10 constructed response, 5 comprehensive questions and 10 numerical problems. Drafts for the academic review.

The book prints no MCQ key; the keys are worked out from the chapter: 1 c, 2 d, 3 d, 4 d, 5 c, 6 d, 7 d, 8 b, 9 a, 10 c, 11 b. MCQ 6 keyed (d) 'all of the above' (wave nature plus field focusing; the chapter names electromagnetic lenses only, electrostatic focusing is general knowledge). MCQ 10 keyed (c) from Section 18.8 ('electrons are not present inside atomic nucleus').

Owner rule BOOK-CORRECTION-01 applied: all printed questions, options and printed answers keep the book's wording; checkpoints carry no book_errors field, so each wording error has a Book correction / Kitab ki ghalti box after the question, and the Roman Urdu prompt line gives the correct reading.

Wording errors (callout boxes): Short 18.1 'pocket' -> 'packet'; Short 18.7 'Will high frequency light has more number of electrons' -> 'eject more electrons' ('has' -> 'have'); Short 18.10 'witch' -> 'which' (shift = Compton shift); CRQ 18.3 'form light' -> 'from light', 'elections' -> 'electrons'; CRQ 18.8 'driving' -> 'deriving', 'does' -> 'do'; Comprehensive 18.3 'varies elements' -> 'various elements'; Comprehensive 18.4 'the transmission of electron microscope' -> 'the transmission electron microscope'; Numerical 18.6 'associate' -> 'associated'.

Grammar-only slips kept as printed without a box (correct reading in the Roman Urdu line only): MCQ 18.6 'An electron microscope employ the principle: (a) electron have a wave nature' (employs; electrons have); Short 18.8 'when does it behaves as consisted of particles' (behave as if it consisted); CRQ 18.5 'How can spectrum of hydrogen atom contains' (contain).
Book correction, numerical 18.2: printed 4.5 x 10^14 Hz; f = 3 x 10^-18 J / 6.63 x 10^-34 J s = 4.5 x 10^15 Hz.
Book correction, numerical 18.3: the question also prints '(124 nm)', contradicting the printed answer 1.99 x 10^-7 m (199 nm, which is right); 124 nm is the wavelength for 10 eV.

Numerical 18.7: the printed answers 6 x 10^2 m s^-1 and 6 x 10^2 m follow from dx dp >= h/4pi (beyond the chapter). The chapter's dx dp ~ h (Eq. 18.14, Example 18.4) gives 7.3 x 10^3 m s^-1 and about 7 x 10^3 m. Both workings are given, with a Book correction box; the Roman Urdu advises the chapter's method in exams.

Numericals 18.1, 18.4, 18.9, 18.10 agree with the printed answers; 18.5 gives 274 nm with h = 6.63 x 10^-34 and c = 3 x 10^8 (book 273 nm, precise constants; agrees); 18.6 agrees with p rounded to 1.27 x 10^-23 (unrounded 5.24 x 10^-11 m); 18.8 (ii) gives 6.28 x 10^3 m s^-1 (book 6.29 x 10^3, rounding).

Beyond the chapter: CRQ 18.1 (energy bands in solids), CRQ 18.3 (X-rays from inner-shell transitions), CRQ 18.6 (relativistic GeV energy estimate; the chapter states 'of the order of GeV'), Comprehensive 18.4 differences table (vacuum, specimens, glass vs magnetic lenses, optical resolution), Comprehensive 18.3 sodium 589 nm example, Numerical 18.7 h/4pi form; Short 18.5 uses an assumed tennis-ball mass and speed (0.06 kg, 30 m s^-1) as an example.
Questions describing diagrams: none in this exercise; no figures added.
